The background leading to the Rule, in short, is that the respondent No. 3-Islami Bank Bangladesh Limited, Bhola Branch on 20-5-2007 as plaintiff flied a suit before the Joint district Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Bhola (hereinafter referred to as Adalat) against the petitioner and others for realization of loan money of Tk. 4,52,49,912 by selling mortgaged properties. The case was contested by the defendant Nos. 1-5/7-12 by filing joint written statement denying all the material averments of the plaint. Subsequently, the suit was decreed on contest against the defendant Nos. 1-5/7-12 and ex-parte against the rest. The respondent- bank then put the decree into execution in execution Case No. 20 of 2010. In that Execution Case the petitioner filed an application on 8-5-2011 (Annexure-D) praying for permission to sell some of the mortgaged properties on private negotiations at a higher price. The Adalat on hearing rejected the application by the impugned order No. 14 on 8-5-2011 (Annexure-D-1) against, which the petitioner moved this Division and obtained the present Rule. Be it mentioned that the Rule has two parts, one, challenging the impugned order and the second one is against the publication of auction notices in -one local daily Ajker Bhola on 20-4-2011 and in the Daily Nayadiganta on 22-4-2011 sought to be declared without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 

 "The learned Judge, Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka being the concerned executing Court is directed to grant certificate under Order XXI, rule 83(2) of the Code allowing the petitioner to sell the schedule property of Artha Execution Case No. 682 of within a time to be specified by the Adalat. If the petitioner fails to sell the property under sale within the specified time and to deposit the requisite amount of money in the Court for satisfying the decree within the specified time, the execution case will proceed in accordance with law." 

 7. Order XXI, rule 83 of the Code does not come into conflict with any of the provisions of Artha Rin Adalat Ain (hereinafter referred to as Ain) and as such applicable in an Execution proceeding under the Ain. While arriving at such a decision this Division Bench also took an account of section 26 of the Ain which made the Code of Civil Procedure applicable in execution proceeding so far the relevant provisions of the Code is not inconsistent with the provision of the Ain. In the case in hand we have observed the decree was passed back in the year 2010 and the Execution Case proceeded as usual at the behest of the respondent bank. In the proceeding the petitioner made an application under Order XXI, rule 83 and made a prayer for selling of the schedule mortgaged property in a private negotiation on the basis of some reason stated in the application (Annexure-D). the Adalat gave a decision on the issue pointedly by stating since there is a specific provision to dispose of an execution case available in the Ain itself, the application should be rejected and accordingly the same was rejected by the order impugned against. 

 (1)	Where an order for the sale of immovable property has been made, if the judgment- debtor can satisfy the Court that there is reason to believe that the amount of the decree may be raised by the mortgage or lease or private sale of such property or 

 9. On a plain reading of the said provision we have found that upon the satisfaction of the Court a private sale of the mortgaged property to satisfy the decreetal amount can be allowed to the Judgment debtor by the Court. A reasonable time for so doing only to be given. In the decision reported in 16 MLR as referred to above and in an unreported decision of Writ Petition No. 302 of 2010 the question has been answered in affirmative. The Order impugned against is not at all in terms of the provision of the Code as it could be found. Under these circumstances, we are of the view that the ends of justice would be best served if the petitioner has been given a chance to pursue his wish by which the decreetal amount may be paid of by private selling of the mortgaged property, and in all fairness that should be allowed. Of course time should be reasonable as it has been allowed in the above mentioned two decisions of this Division.
